option_relations.rationale: The vignette and imaging studies suggest follicular thyroid cells, not papillary thyroid carcinoma.
The presence of follicular thyroid cells in the goiter and manubrial lesion, along with the lytic lesion replacing the manubrium, is consistent with metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma.
Metastatic thyroid carcinoma is a broader term that encompasses follicular thyroid carcinoma with bone metastasis.

The description of follicular thyroid cells infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae is consistent with follicular thyroid carcinoma with manubrial invasion, which is equivalent to follicular thyroid carcinoma with bone metastasis.
